description: Ordered Chromium integration patches for the Project Seoul native product. Materialize native/seoul/ first, then apply. The series wires the native services and product surfaces into Chromium and makes Seoul's vertical workspace shell the fresh-profile default.

entrySchema.rationale: why it is necessary and which upstream alternative was rejected
entrySchema.baseRevision: full Chromium SHA this patch is authored against; must equal manifest baseRevision
entrySchema.order: unique ascending integer giving application order
entrySchema.file: patch file path relative to patchDir
affectedPaths: upstream src-relative paths the patch touches
entrySchema.sha256: lowercase hex sha256 of the patch file
entrySchema.applyVerify: command/strategy proving the patch applies cleanly (git apply --check)
entrySchema.reverseVerify: command/strategy proving the patch reverses cleanly (git apply -R --check)
entrySchema.reviewable: true once the patch is independently reviewable in isolation

patches.description: Wire Seoul organization, lifecycle, command, projection, shell, product-runtime, and canvas targets into //chrome/browser (deps + allow_circular_includes_from); register SeoulOrganizationServiceFactory and SeoulRuntimeServiceFactory once at profile-service init; register Seoul projection and shell against VerticalTabStripRegionView only AFTER RootTabCollectionNode::Init() and unregister them at the start of ResetTabStrip; expose a production GetSeoulRootNode() accessor (no testing-only accessor in production); forward durable collapse state separately from compact-mode hover presentation so the full tab/project hierarchy reveals without mutating preferences; register the SeoulCanvasUIConfig (chrome://seoul-canvas), expose its typed Mojo factory only to that trusted controller, generate and merge its resources into Chromium's runtime resources.pak, register one regular-profile kSeoulCanvas side-panel entry per window, and pass the browser binding to the Shell so its launcher opens that exact entry; add a localized, DLP-gated Preview Link command to the regular-profile link context menu and route its exact source WebContents to PreviewHostService; and wire the Seoul in-process browser-test source_sets into //chrome/test:browser_tests.
patches.rationale: Chromium-facing Seoul glue includes //chrome/browser headers and must use the browser_public_dependencies circular-implementation pattern. A single patch avoids duplicate lifecycle linkage (organization already depends on lifecycle transitively), keeps factory registration in one place, and adds Preview at Chromium's existing typed link-command seam instead of intercepting or guessing page gestures.
patches.applyVerify: materialize.sh apply; git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0001-seoul-native-core.patch

patches.description: Enable Chromium's vertical-tabs infrastructure and its fresh-profile preferences by default so every normal Seoul window starts on the product's vertical workspace shell without a hidden command-line flag or onboarding toggle; update the upstream controller tests to assert and explicitly isolate the new defaults.
patches.rationale: Seoul's shell is registered on VerticalTabStripRegionView. Leaving upstream's feature and preference defaults off would ship a working implementation that fresh users never see. A separate, reviewable defaults patch keeps this intentional product fork policy distinct from the mechanical integration patch and preserves the user's ability to switch layouts later.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0002-seoul-product-defaults.patch after applying 0001-seoul-native-core.patch

patches.description: Carry Seoul's opaque durable tab-membership id through Chromium's existing per-tab session extra-data channel, include it in full session-command rebuilds, and restore it onto WebContents before the tab enters TabStripModel.
patches.rationale: Chromium creates new window and tab SessionIDs during relaunch, rebuilds session commands from BrowserLiveTabContext, and does not expose generic restored tab extra-data after WebContents construction. Two narrow typed hooks beside Chromium's existing Glic extra-data snapshot/restore hooks let Seoul atomically rebind organization state without persisting page data, guessing by URL, or creating duplicate memberships.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0003-seoul-session-membership-restore.patch after applying 0001-seoul-native-core.patch and 0002-seoul-product-defaults.patch

patches.description: Expose a window-local vertical-tab reveal-on-hover setter so Seoul can apply durable Workspace and Scene presentation policy without mutating Chromium's profile-wide stock preference.
patches.rationale: Chromium's public SetExpandOnHoverEnabled method writes a profile preference observed by every browser window. Seoul compact mode is Workspace/window scoped, so using that setter would make independent windows fight each other. The narrow setter updates the existing per-controller state and notifications without introducing a second presentation owner.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0004-seoul-window-local-compact-hover.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0003

patches.description: Add a localized Boost row to HTTP(S) site controls, accept the exact New Boost omnibox command without navigating or searching, and preserve each matching Boost's automatic-dark preference through Chromium WebPreferences recomputation and navigation.
patches.rationale: Site controls and the omnibox are Chromium-owned discovery surfaces, while Boost state and editing remain owned by Seoul's profile runtime and trusted Canvas. Two narrow entry calls keep both surfaces on one eligibility/editor path, and the WebPreferences hook makes automatic dark mode a per-tab, per-site behavior instead of mutating Chrome's profile-wide force-dark preference.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0005-seoul-boost-entry-points.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0004

patches.description: Move Chromium's real native omnibox and core navigation into Seoul's vertical rail as a two-row address block, hide stock organizer/tab-search chrome, flush page contents against the visible rail width (no invented seam), suppress the integrated-rail trailing outline, clear Mac traffic-light band above the address row, and route regular-profile NTP rewrites to chrome://seoul-canvas/.
patches.rationale: Keeping a full-width Chromium toolbar, responsive icon overflow, and Google NTP beside a custom vertical shell leaves the product visually and structurally Chromium-first. Reusing the native location bar preserves security and focus behavior while Commands owns secondary browser actions; placing the NTP decision in Chromium's canonical rewrite path covers startup and chrome://newtab rather than only one Browser call site.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0006-seoul-integrated-vertical-shell.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0005

patches.description: Hide Chromium VerticalTabStripTopContainer (View Organizer / Tab Search) and its separator at construction time so stock rail chrome never paints above Seoul's product shell.
patches.rationale: UpdateSeoulSidebarPresentation can reinforce the hide, but construction-time visibility is required so organizer/tab-search never flash or consume flex space before the first Seoul presentation update.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0007-seoul-hide-stock-rail-chrome.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0006

patches.description: Match Zen's Chromium-hosted product surface: 60px collapsed and 500px maximum rail geometry, an active Space row between pinned and regular tabs, transparent labeled New Tab control, 8px content separation with rounded web surfaces, a centered native floating omnibox while editing, and restoration of Chromium's normal New Tab routing instead of forcing Canvas.
patches.rationale: The product must feel like Zen without replacing Chromium's browser semantics. Reusing and temporarily reparenting Chromium's native LocationBarView preserves security state, autocomplete, focus, and navigation; extending the existing vertical-tab layout preserves native tabs and drag behavior; content insets and rounded WebView holders create Zen's separated page surface without a web-shell approximation.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0008-seoul-zen-product-surface.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0007

patches.description: Replace remaining Chromium product identity with Seoul, establish a cohesive light/dark rail and canvas palette across frame, tabs, toolbar, omnibox, and New Tab surfaces, retain a visible Zen-style resting address pill, strip Google furniture from the fallback New Tab document, suppress Chromium's missing-Google-API-key warning, and keep the command bar focused on local history and navigation rather than remote trends or Gemini promotion.
patches.rationale: Layout parity alone still reads as Chromium when stock branding, blue/system control colors, Google New Tab furniture, API-key warnings, or editorial search content remains visible. A final product mixer preserves Chromium's platform plumbing while giving Seoul authoritative styling, and provider-level filtering prevents server experiments from reintroducing foreign product content.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0009-seoul-product-identity-and-palette.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0008

patches.description: Replace Chromium's app-bundle, default-favicon, browser-resource, shortcut, authentication-dialog, Linux launcher, ChromeOS, and updater icons with Seoul's deterministic native product mark; ensure macOS reads Seoul's ICNS instead of the inherited Chromium asset catalog.
patches.rationale: A renamed app still reads as Chromium when its Dock icon and New Tab favicon retain the blue Chromium mark. Seoul-owned vector, PNG, and ICNS assets remove those last high-salience identity leaks while preserving Chromium's favicon and bundle-loading behavior.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0010-seoul-product-iconography.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0009 and materializing native/seoul

patches.description: Replace the default-search-provider advertising in Seoul's resting address pill with the neutral localized prompt “Search or enter an address,” while preserving keyword, AI-mode, and contextual-task placeholders.
patches.rationale: The integrated rail must not display “Search Google” as product chrome. A dedicated localized Seoul string keeps the command/address field provider-neutral without changing the user's configured search engine or URL/search behavior.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0011-seoul-neutral-address-prompt.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0010

patches.description: Keep Seoul's revealed compact sidebar open for one second after pointer exit, while still canceling an uncommitted reveal immediately when the pointer leaves before expansion.
patches.rationale: Zen's compact-mode sidebar deliberately lingers after hover so users can cross small gaps without the rail snapping shut. Chromium collapses its stock hover rail immediately; a Seoul-only delay matches the current Zen interaction cadence without changing stock vertical-tab behavior.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0012-seoul-zen-compact-hover-timing.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0011

patches.description: Replace the permanent rail address pill with an Arc-style transient command surface; integrate macOS traffic lights and navigation into one 38px header row; center and animate Zen's 62px floating omnibox over the page canvas; preserve visible prompts, unclipped suggestions, one-Escape dismissal, first-tab Cmd+L behavior, and Seoul's Cmd+Shift+K command palette routing; and finish Seoul product identity on native window titles and the version surface.
patches.rationale: A permanently visible Chromium address field, detached search glyph, oversized caption-button band, clipped popup cutout, or Chromium wordmark breaks the Arc/Zen product composition. Reparenting Chromium's native LocationBarView only while focused retains its security, autocomplete, accessibility, and navigation semantics while Seoul owns the command-surface geometry and interaction cadence.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0013-seoul-arc-command-surface.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0012

patches.description: Finish the Zen/Arc native surface by aligning macOS traffic lights and navigation on one compact row, removing the floating address identity artifact, capping the unified action surface at 750px, keeping compact hover expansion overlay-only, and completing Seoul identity in settings, WebUI logos, document UTIs, and an independently owned macOS Safe Storage item that never probes Chromium credentials.
patches.rationale: The product cannot ship with a duplicated caption inset, a raised search glyph, page reflow on compact hover, Chromium labels in user-facing surfaces, or keychain access to another application's credential. These changes preserve Chromium's native security and navigation behavior while keeping the visible shell and credential ownership consistently Seoul; a recording fake regression test locks the keychain path to one Seoul lookup and a Seoul-only write.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0014-seoul-zen-layout-branding-and-migration.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0013

patches.description: Enable Chromium's native macOS glass frame by default for Seoul, remove the integrated rail toolbar's opaque background slab, and replace opaque green interaction fills with Zen-derived active, hover, and selected-tab layers precomposited over their native backgrounds plus contrast-aware text and URL recipes.
patches.rationale: Zen's macOS surface lets native under-window material carry the frame and composes interaction states from low-alpha currentColor layers. Chromium also consumes its shared background tokens in contrast recipes, so Seoul precomposites those layers to opaque token values while preserving their rendered appearance; keeping raw alpha there violates the color-provider contract, while disabling glass or painting a CustomCornersBackground behind the integrated navigation row blocks the native material.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0015-seoul-native-material-and-state-colors.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0014

patches.description: Resolve Seoul's inner content radius at runtime to 10 DIP on macOS 26 and newer, 6 DIP on older macOS, 5 DIP on Windows and Linux, and 6 DIP on other platforms; apply that value consistently to content, DevTools, scrims, footer, overlays, and split corner masks; and use a 12 DIP vertical-tab radius on macOS while retaining Chromium's 8 DIP value elsewhere.
patches.rationale: Zen's content canvas and vertical tabs use platform-specific geometry. One resolved content radius must feed every docked DevTools and split-view corner combination so adjacent surfaces stay flush rather than exposing mismatched clipping or square gaps.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0016-seoul-platform-content-and-tab-radii.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0015

patches.description: Complete Seoul's source-matched Zen interaction and visual fidelity: bind Compact Mode to Zen's exact Command/Ctrl+S shortcut, use a 5-DIP hidden Compact edge and 60-DIP ordinary collapsed rail, render normal vertical tabs as Zen's 40-DIP rows with 36-DIP inset surfaces, eight-DIP corners, and selected shadow, clip retained sidebar controls only at the integrated Compact endpoint, keep the rail full-height through hover, preserve 250 ms reveal and 150 ms exit-hold animation continuity, restore macOS traffic lights correctly, preserve Zen's selected command-surface contrast, distinguish synthetic startup new-tab placeholders from ordinary and restored tabs, retire placeholder presentation on same-tab navigation, keep real site favicons and Zen's neutral globe fallback instead of product branding, preserve append-at-end link drops after moving New Tab above regular tabs, ignore stale compositor callbacks after animation cancellation, install dedicated Seoul toolbar vectors, harden shutdown ordering and command surfaces, and force mock keychain storage for every non-official macOS build.
patches.rationale: The earlier structural patches established Seoul's shell, but visual review exposed a blank top band, a permanent icon rail, oversized and weakly inset tab surfaces, retained controls leaking over Compact content, low-contrast selected command rows, duplicated new-tab rows, a stale floating omnibox, product logos leaking into New Tab and favicon-less page rows, glyph substitutions, traffic-light jumps, development keychain prompts, New Tab link drops routed to index zero, and a stale animation callback crash during restore. This cumulative patch ports Zen's measured compact and normal-tab geometry, timing, shortcut, selected-state, shadow, and neutral tab-favicon behavior onto Chromium-native views while retaining Chromium's tab, navigation, drag/drop, accessibility, and security models; explicit startup provenance and fail-open rules prevent synthetic placeholder state from leaking into restored or user-created tabs.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0017-seoul-zen-interaction-and-visual-fidelity.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0016

patches.description: Port current Zen's download-origin motion onto Chromium's native download-start lifecycle: animate a themed token from the initiating cursor position to the visible downloads control or a lower-edge fallback target, support left and right rails, expose bounded profile preferences for enablement and duration, and preserve Chromium's reduced-motion, restored-download, visibility, and download-state gates.
patches.rationale: Seoul previously inherited Chromium's straight toolbar-only download animation, which did not match Zen's curved, scaling one-second token or its temporary lower-edge target when the downloads control is absent. Reusing DownloadToolbarUIController's existing fresh-download notification preserves Chromium's ownership and safety behavior while the Seoul-owned Views implementation supplies the source-matched visual motion without renderer script or a second download model.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0018-seoul-download-origin-animation.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0017

patches.description: Match current Zen's Single Toolbar URL treatment by showing the formatted host at 70% text strength while the field is at rest, then revealing Chromium's full-strength editing URL as soon as the floating omnibox receives focus; expose the behavior as an enabled-by-default profile preference and retain normal URL presentation in horizontal, Multiple, Collapsed, app, and popup windows.
patches.rationale: Replacing the text field contents directly would corrupt selection, copy, navigation, accessibility, and security behavior. This patch instead activates Chromium's existing display-URL host-trimming seam only for a normal browser whose vertical Single Toolbar is actually visible, applies Zen's resting opacity through the native emphasis path, and uses OmniboxEditModel's native unelision path on focus so Chromium remains the sole owner of canonical URL semantics.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0019-seoul-domain-only-resting-url.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0018

patches.description: Register Seoul's profile-keyed native blocker before profile creation, place its browser-process URLLoaderFactory proxy ahead of Chromium's extension, sign-in, and enterprise request-factory chain for document, worker, and service-worker subresources, gate frame-associated WS/WSS handshakes asynchronously while preserving Chromium's extension WebRequest continuation, and add a deferred top-level NavigationThrottle that rechecks redirects and fails blocked pages with ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT.
patches.rationale: A Chromium-native blocker must make its allow/block decision before a supported request reaches the network while preserving Chromium's URLLoader, redirect, response, WebSocket, extension-proxy, and navigation semantics. Registering the keyed-service factory at Chromium's canonical profile-factory seam, appending the tested Seoul proxy at WillCreateURLLoaderFactory, using Chromium's dedicated CreateWebSocket interception seam, and registering a separate NavigationThrottle for primary-main-frame requests are the smallest browser-process integrations; renderer script, DevTools interception, and a second network stack were rejected because they miss workers, sockets, or top-level documents, race page execution, or bypass Chromium's request lifecycle.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0020-seoul-native-adblock-network-hook.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0019

patches.description: Add two dedicated Chromium website-setting types for Seoul's native blocker: a profile-local persistent per-site mode override and a separate profile-local expiring temporary-disable marker; register their top-origin-only, non-incognito-inheriting schemas, exhaustive WebUI entries, and stable UMA enum values.
patches.rationale: Blocker mode and temporary disable have different persistence semantics. Storing both in one record would let expiration remove the persistent mode, while reusing an unrelated permission type would corrupt Chromium's permission UI and policy behavior. Two unsyncable generic dictionary-backed website settings use Chromium's existing scoped preference provider and expiration metadata without introducing a second site-preference database or violating WebsiteSettingsRegistry's sync contract.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0021-seoul-adblock-site-settings.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0020

patches.description: Register a document-scoped Seoul cosmetic-filter Mojo host for every RenderFrame, allocate a fixed Seoul isolated-world id in the synchronized C++ and Android registries, construct the bounded CSS-only renderer agent for every frame, link its Seoul-owned renderer target, and compile its renderer lifecycle coverage into Chromium's browser-test target.
patches.rationale: Cosmetic filtering must hide first-party and dynamically inserted ad elements in main frames and cross-origin subframes without trusting renderer-supplied URLs, blocking a browser thread on Rust, injecting remotely supplied JavaScript, or colliding with Chromium and extension isolated worlds. A document-bound browser interface derives the committed URL and profile settings from RenderFrameHost, dispatches all Rust work asynchronously, and returns selectors only; a fixed isolated-world MutationObserver batches bounded class/id discovery while user-origin stylesheets provide native CSS hiding with prerender and BFCache lifecycle guards. Brave's synchronous URL-resource IPC and remote scriptlet/procedural execution were intentionally rejected for this hardened CSS-only stage.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0022-seoul-adblock-cosmetic-filtering.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0021

patches.description: Register Seoul's signed filter-list package with Chromium's ComponentUpdateService, persist the last verified ready path and version in Local State for profile startup, and fan out verified component activation through the existing profile-keyed blocker service.
patches.rationale: Production browser-vetted lists require Chromium's CRX signature verification and update scheduler rather than a profile downloader or a fake embedded key. The component remains disabled when no owner-supplied public-key hash is configured; when configured, the installer requires encrypted transport, verifies bounded package structure, and delegates full manifest, payload-hash, parse, engine-build, atomic-swap, and last-known-good validation to the profile-owned FilterListManager.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0023-seoul-adblock-component-updater.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0022

patches.description: Register Seoul's $csp response throttle for eligible document and subdocument navigations in the Chromium content browser client, so filter-list $csp rules reach the navigation loader.
patches.rationale: Navigation responses are produced by browser-created loaders and are the only place a $csp directive can be attached before Chromium parses the header block into URLResponseHead::parsed_headers, which is what actually enforces policy. The throttle declines every request that is not an eligible frame navigation and every profile without a blocker, so non-document loads pay nothing. The generated policy is always appended as an additional policy: CSP enforces every delivered policy, so an injected directive can restrict but never relax the site's own. Rewriting or replacing the site header was rejected for exactly that reason.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0024-seoul-adblock-csp-response-filter.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0023

patches.description: Four re-entrancy and hosting guards in the Seoul shell integration: a generation counter so an animation subscriber may start a replacement motion from its own kEnded notification, a reparenting flag so toolbar removal notifications do not drive sidebar presentation through a stale View::parent(), an exemption so the omnibox popup invariant is not evaluated while the Seoul floating command surface is being installed, and an expand-on-hover rule that ignores focus inside the hosted toolbar.
patches.rationale: Each guard fixes a defect reachable from ordinary interaction. View::DoRemoveChildView de-registers a child from its parent's layout manager before dispatching removal notifications but clears View::parent() only afterwards, so an observer that re-enters sidebar presentation calls SetVisible() on a toolbar the layout manager no longer tracks, which CHECKs in LayoutManagerBase::ViewVisibilitySet; neither parent() nor children() is a valid liveness proxy inside that window, so BrowserView flags the reparent instead. The vertical rail chains an expand-on-hover reveal off the end of a collapse, so clearing motion state unconditionally on kEnded erases the replacement motion's state while its animator still runs, leaving IsAnimating() false for a live animation and snapping layout to the end value. The omnibox invariant describes widget-backed presentation only, which is why the existing WebUI popups are already exempt. The fourth guard fixes a defect that made the sidebar impossible to collapse. Upstream holds the rail open while focus is inside it, so keyboard tab navigation cannot collapse the strip out from under the user; that rule assumes the rail holds tabs and nothing else. Seoul hosts the toolbar inside it, so the omnibox - which holds focus in a new window and after every Cmd+L - pinned the rail at its full width with the mouse nowhere near it, and RequestCollapse became a silent no-op. Focus in the hosted toolbar is therefore not treated as focus in the tab strip.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0025-seoul-shell-reentrancy-guards.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0024

patches.description: Skip Chromium's macOS code-sign clone in component builds, where the cloned bundle cannot resolve the shared libraries the executable links against.
patches.rationale: A component build keeps its shared libraries in the build directory rather than inside the app bundle, and the main executable reaches them through an @loader_path/../../.. rpath that only resolves while the app runs from its own build output. CodeSignCloneManager re-executes the browser from a copy of the bundle in a temporary directory, where that rpath resolves to nothing, so dyld fails to load libc++_chrome.dylib before any Chrome code runs: no log line, no crash handler, and macOS reports only "Seoul cannot be opened because of a problem". The clone exists solely to keep the code signature stable across auto-updates, which a component development build does not have, so skipping it costs nothing. Upstream already makes the same trade for Chrome for Testing immediately below the guarded code. Release (non-component) builds keep the clone.
patches.applyVerify: git -C $SEOUL_CHROMIUM_ROOT/src apply --check native/patches/chromium/0026-seoul-component-build-no-code-sign-clone.patch after applying patches 0001 through 0025

patches.description: Register the first-run WebUI at chrome://seoul-welcome: its host, its Mojo binder, its grit id range, its resource pack, and the Lit visibility entry its resources build against.
patches.rationale: A WebUI only exists once Chromium's config map knows its host, and a WebUI resource target can only use the packaged Lit build after being named in that target's visibility list - both of which live in upstream files. The Canvas took the same two lines in 0001; this adds the equivalent pair for the welcome surface rather than growing the foundational patch, so the first-run flow stays independently reviewable and reversible. Rejected alternative: hosting onboarding inside the existing Canvas WebUI, which needs no upstream change but contradicts the Welcome/onboarding row of docs/product/zen-chromium-parity.md and would make the whole Canvas runtime a first-run dependency.
patches.applyVerify: git apply --check

patches.description: Paint the browser chrome in Seoul's own warm palette instead of Zen's cool neutral, so the frame matches the first-party surfaces it contains.
patches.rationale: The chrome resolved to #F0F0F4 / #17171A - the unthemed macOS material copied from Zen - while every surface Seoul actually renders (the Canvas, the first-run flow) is warm cream at #F2F1EB / #171715. The window and its contents therefore read as two applications beside each other, which is the single most visible reason the product looked unfinished. These are the same hex values the WebUI uses, so the two halves cannot drift again. Copying a competitor's neutral was also the wrong target: Seoul is not a Zen skin. Rejected alternative: restyling each shell view individually, which would have touched 46 call sites across four files and left the tokens Chromium itself paints with - frame, toolbar, tab backgrounds - still cool.
patches.applyVerify: git apply --check

patches.description: Fix the reload arrowhead, add the collapse half of the sidebar glyph pair, and give the toolbar's sidebar control a Seoul icon instead of Chromium's stock one.
patches.rationale: The reload arrowhead was three points drawn with STROKE, which renders two open segments - a stray tick beside the ring rather than an arrow. Closed and filled. The sidebar glyph existed only in its expand direction, so the toolbar control fell back to kLeftPanelCloseIcon, a bare square and bar from an unrelated family; the pair now mirrors on the same frame and divider. Safe in the toolbar specifically: it already links chrome/app/vector_icons for kSeoulReloadIcon. Rejected alternative: theming the vertical tab strip's own collapse button in chrome/browser/ui/tabs, which segfaults on first paint - those icons are declared with a plain extern and no COMPONENT_EXPORT, so a component outside chrome/ that names one resolves to null at load.
patches.applyVerify: git apply --check

patches.description: Give the page the same gap on all four sides: drop the macOS leading-edge special case and suppress the top-container separator when Seoul's rail owns the chrome.
patches.rationale: Measured against the running product, the page sat 9 DIP from the top, 8 from the right and bottom, and 6 from the rail. The leading six came from a special case asserting that Zen's splitter occupied the other two, but Seoul's resize area is kViewIgnoredByLayoutKey - an invisible drag target that consumes no layout space - so nothing occupied them. The extra top DIP was the top-container separator, a one-DIP rule whose height is added to the contents origin; the rail owns the toolbar and draws its own boundary, so that rule has nothing left to separate. Both removed, and all four gaps now measure 8.
patches.applyVerify: git apply --check

patches.description: Give a tab opened in an isolated Space its own StoragePartition, so cookies and site data cannot cross between Spaces.
patches.rationale: Chromium already supports a SiteInstance pinned to a fixed StoragePartition that survives navigation, which is exactly the lifetime a container needs; the only missing piece is deciding which partition a new tab starts in. CreateTargetContents() is the one place that choice is made, so Seoul is consulted there and returns null whenever the active Space is not isolated, leaving Chromium's ordinary selection untouched. The opener branch is left ahead of it deliberately: a tab opened from another tab inherits its opener's SiteInstance and therefore its partition, so following a link out of a container keeps the user inside it. Deciding per-site through GetStoragePartitionConfigForSite() was rejected because a container is a property of the Space the tab belongs to, not of the site being visited.
patches.applyVerify: git apply --check

patches.description: Keep every character the user types: never let the floating-omnibox reparent, or a presentation callback, overwrite or drop an edit in progress; and let a query that names no Seoul command reach the configured default search provider.
patches.rationale: Seoul expands the docked Single Toolbar field into a centred floating surface, and that expansion reparents the real LocationBarView. Views has no move-without-blur: AddChildViewAt() routes through DoRemoveChildView(), Widget::ViewHierarchyChanged() calls FocusManager::ViewRemoved() for any removal including a same-widget move, and focus is cleared. Three consequences are fixed here rather than papered over with a delay. First, the transition now runs on the keystroke that begins editing, before the character is inserted, so the field being moved still holds the page URL and the restored whole-URL selection is exactly what that keystroke should replace; entering afterwards reparented a field already holding the first character and re-selected it, so the second keystroke overwrote the first. Second, when the transition is reached with an edit already in progress (paste, IME, drop), focus is restored with RequestFocus() and the autocomplete pass restarted, instead of FocusLocation()'s user-initiated path whose Unelide()+SelectAll() would select the in-progress text. Third, docking now refuses to interrupt a focused field with an uncommitted edit, so a completed load or an arriving lifecycle snapshot cannot take the surface away mid-query; the layout-mode reparent, which must move the location bar with its toolbar, opts out explicitly and restores focus itself. Separately, the command surface no longer swallows Return for a query that names no command: fuzzy subsequence ranking is right for ordering rows and far too permissive for deciding that Return should run a command instead of searching, so intent is now a distinct question (exact, prefix, or word-boundary match), and anything else hands the body and the Return key back to Chromium's omnibox and its configured default search provider. The hardcoded English 'New Boost' text interception in ChromeOmniboxClient is removed for the same reason: it silently swallowed a search for that phrase.
patches.applyVerify: git apply --check

patches.description: Put a paintbrush at the right of the address field that opens the Boost editor for the page, which is where Arc puts the same action and the only way the feature is discoverable.
patches.rationale: Before this the Boost editor could only be reached from the command surface, so nobody who did not already know the feature existed could find it. Arc reaches its editor from a paintbrush in the Site Control Panel at the right of the URL bar; this is the same affordance in the same place, opening the same editor through the existing OpenBoostEditorForWebContents entry point rather than a second path. It is a plain ImageButton in the location bar's trailing decorations, so it inherits the field's own layout and does not disturb Chromium's identity, permission or page-action chrome. Two visibility rules keep it honest: it is hidden while the omnibox is floating, because at that point the user is editing a query rather than looking at a page and there is no site to restyle; and it is hidden for anything that is not http(s), because a Boost is scoped to a web origin and there is nothing to scope it to otherwise.
patches.applyVerify: git apply --check
